pointers.sentence: Each turns on whether every alias in the class's `databases` has `BaseDatabaseFeatures.supports_transactions`, and all but `_fixture_teardown` on whether each has `BaseDatabaseFeatures.uses_savepoints` too, as `TestCase._databases_support_transactions` and `TestCase._databases_support_savepoints` ask (`django/test/testcases.py:connections_support_transactions`, `django/test/testcases.py:connections_support_savepoints`).

Each turns on whether every alias in the class's `databases` has `BaseDatabaseFeatures.supports_transactions`, and all but `_fixture_teardown` on whether each has `BaseDatabaseFeatures.uses_savepoints` too, as `TestCase._databases_support_transactions` and `TestCase._databases_support_savepoints` ask (`django/test/testcases.py:connections_support_transactions`, `django/test/testcases.py:connections_support_savepoints`).
SQLite, PostgreSQL and Oracle have both; MySQL too, unless its engine is MyISAM (`django/db/backends/mysql/features.py:DatabaseFeatures.supports_transactions`).

The class's block sent `"BEGIN"` on entering, before any write: SQLite's backend begins a transaction with that statement, followed by the `"transaction_mode"` of its `"OPTIONS"` where one is set (`django/db/backends/sqlite3/base.py:DatabaseWrapper._start_transaction_under_autocommit`).

`TestCase.setUpClass` first calls the parent's: `SimpleTestCase.setUpClass` enters the class's overridden settings and guards the aliases it does not name, and `TransactionTestCase.setUpClass` runs no `_pre_setup` for a `TestCase` (`django/test/testcases.py:TransactionTestCase.setUpClass`).
A project's `setUpClass` that raises after calling the parent's leaves the transaction open; Django's documentation warns of a segmentation fault on some platforms (`docs/topics/testing/tools.txt`).
`TestData` is a descriptor with a `__get__` and no `__set__` (`django/test/testcases.py:TestData`).

Inside the class's blocks, `Atomic.__enter__` makes each new block a savepoint (`django/test/testcases.py:TestCase._fixture_setup`; [Transactions: autocommit, `atomic` and savepoints](../connections/atomic.md#entering-a-block-atomic__enter)).
Nothing is wrapped in `TestData`; Django's documentation notes the speed lost without transactions (`docs/topics/testing/tools.txt`).
`TestCase._fixture_teardown`, where the databases have transactions, goes through the class's aliases in reverse order (`django/test/testcases.py:TestCase._fixture_teardown`).
The release notes of Django 1.10, which added the check, give its purpose as catching bugs (`docs/releases/1.10.txt`).

Then `"PRAGMA foreign_key_check"` found the row, SQLite's `check_constraints` raised (`django/db/backends/sqlite3/base.py:DatabaseWrapper.check_constraints`), and `SimpleTestCase._setup_and_call` added an error to the same test, the E.

`TestCase.tearDownClass`, where the databases have both features, rolls the class's blocks back, ending each transaction, and closes every connection that was opened; in every case it then calls the parent's (`django/test/testcases.py:TestCase.tearDownClass`).
